title: Pods stuck in Pending
scenario: "After the last release some pods stayed Pending for minutes and the HPA shows <unknown>. We have two small nodes — make the workloads fit and autoscale." — SRE on call
mission: Diagnose scheduling with requests/limits and allocatable capacity, and make the HPA read real metrics.

steps.title: Look at the nodes
steps.detail: Allocated resources section of each node.

steps.title: Look at the HPA
steps.detail: Targets must show a percentage, not <unknown>.

steps.title: Change through Git
steps.detail: If requests need tuning, change chart values via PR.

criteria.text: No pods in Pending in the portal namespaces
Every HPA reports current CPU utilisation
Total CPU requests are below 80% of allocatable

expectedResult: Workloads fit with headroom and scale on real metrics.
recovery: HPA <unknown>: containers without CPU requests, or metrics-server not ready.
dont: Do not remove requests to "make it schedule"
Do not kubectl edit the HPA
hints: The scheduler only looks at requests, never at limits or real usage.
kubectl top pods -A shows real usage.

interview.question: Requests vs limits: what does the scheduler use, what does the kubelet enforce?
followUps: What happens when memory exceeds the limit? And CPU?

debrief: Scheduling is by requests; CPU limits throttle, memory limits OOM-kill. HPA needs requests to compute utilisation. On a 2-node cluster leave headroom for surge, system pods and the smoke job.

checker.plan: Read-only: kubectl get pods/hpa -o json, kubectl get nodes -o json (allocatable) and pod requests.

validation.notes: Checker not implemented yet; needs a running cluster.
